research_topic: Will we ever travel at the speed of light?
scope: Massive spacecraft and human/robotic interstellar mission concepts under established physics; no claim that a faster-than-light mechanism exists.

claims.claim: Finite-energy acceleration of a nonzero-rest-mass craft cannot reach c in special relativity.
Directed-energy sails can be modeled at relativistic but subluminal speed; diffraction, material, and ISM constraints are central.
Interstellar gas and dust create velocity-dependent damage and shielding challenges.
Radiation and biological constraints must be treated as mission-level requirements.
No currently verified anomalous-thrust result establishes a route around the relativistic boundary.

prohibited_inferences: A relativistic sail model demonstrates human travel near c.
Time dilation permits a massive craft to attain or exceed c.
A laboratory null result proves every future propulsion idea impossible.
A radiation or shielding model supplies a universal safe-speed threshold.
